verdict.rationale: incident.io's own docs describe key-based alert deduplication: no new alert is created while an alert with the same key is active. They also describe alert grouping, which merges related alerts into one group that is triaged, escalated and attached to an incident once. Together these deliver the core of 'one incident pages one human'. Missing for 10: detail on how grouping rules or time windows are configured, explicit confirmation that a group triggers only a single page, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an SRE, duplicate and related alerts are deduplicated and grouped so one incident pages one human, not fifty

citations.quote: if alert A is received with a deduplication key "x" and alert B with the same deduplication key is received while alert A is still active... no new alert will be created for alert B
Alert grouping groups those related alerts into a single alert group, so you can triage, escalate and attach them to an incident once
a deduplication key is used to uniquely identify alerts and prevent the generation of duplicate alerts
